stages.title: What shifts long-run aggregate supply
stages.sub: Four things that change how much an economy can produce in the long run.

steps.q: Two factories employ the same number of workers, but one factory's workers are far better trained. Which can produce more?
steps.right: The one with better trained workers
steps.wrong: The one with more untrained workers
steps.hint: Same numbers, so what else could make output differ?

steps.right: It rises, and long-run supply shifts right
steps.wrong: It stays the same, as only spending matters
steps.hint: Better trained workers can produce more from the same resources.

steps.q: The newcomers are young and have a wide mix of skills. What happens to the country's long-run productive potential?
steps.right: It rises, as more workers can produce more
steps.wrong: It stays the same, as workers cannot add output

steps.q: A firm must hire extra staff and fill in pages of forms to meet every new rule. What happens to its costs?
steps.right: They rise, using money that could make goods
steps.wrong: They fall, as the rules give clear guidance
steps.hint: The staff and forms have to be paid for.

steps.q: A government cuts red tape so firms spend less time on paperwork. What happens to what the economy can produce in the long run?
steps.right: It rises, as firms spend more on production
steps.wrong: It falls, as firms are less closely controlled
steps.hint: Time and money freed from paperwork can go into making goods.

steps.q: A shop faces new rivals selling the same goods more cheaply. What must it do to keep its customers?
steps.right: Cut its costs and improve how it works
steps.wrong: Ignore them and put up its own prices
steps.hint: A shop that stands still loses customers to cheaper rivals.

steps.q: A government breaks up a monopoly so that many firms compete. What happens to efficiency across the industry?
steps.right: It improves, so more is made from the same resources
steps.wrong: It worsens, as firms waste effort fighting each other
steps.hint: Firms that must compete cannot afford to waste resources.
